subject: Performance dashboard handoff + QBR checklist and owner assignments
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Pierce <jordan.pierce@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance dashboard handoff + QBR checklist and owner assignments

Team — attaching the draft monthly performance dashboard for Acme (attached: 202709_QBR_dashboard_v1.xlsx). I did an initial pass on the usual KPI buckets but want to lock owners and a short remediation plan for the QBR next week. Key highlights pulled from the data: 

- Latency: 95th P50->P95 tilt at 200ms -> 420ms over the last 7 days during peak (seq len spikes).
- Cost: Token spend up 32% month-over-month; ~60% of that attributed to sustained dedicated pool usage in region-us-west.
- Uptime: Two short incidents on 2027-09-04 and 2027-09-10 (5m and 12m) caused by autoscaler flapping during a rolling kernel update.
- Usage: Daily active app sessions up 18%, but request size distribution changed (more long-context eval requests).

Asks before Thursday QBR: 
1) Owners: please confirm who will own each KPI (latency/cost/uptime/usage) and a one-line remediation for any item needing work.
2) Cost anomaly: Vivek, can you validate whether the dedicated pool scaling change last month is responsible for the 32% increase?
3) Latency tracing: Tessa, please attach the top 3 call stacks / model variants by error/latency so we can include them in the readout.
4) Uptime RCA: Irene, can you draft the short-incident RCA (2–3 bullets) for the QBR appendix?
5) External ask: Jordan, if you can confirm whether Acme increased concurrent synthetic tests the week of 9/3, it would help attribution.

I propose a 30-min alignment on Tuesday 09/14 14:00 PT — please RSVP or propose alternate. If you prefer, leave owner replies inline.

Attachments: 202709_QBR_dashboard_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet; tabbed by KPI)

Thanks,
Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Director, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Pierce <jordan.pierce@acme-cloud.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance dashboard handoff + QBR checklist and owner assignments

Thanks Lukas — got the dashboard. Quick answers from our side: 
- We did run an expanded soak test during 9/3–9/5 while validating a feature flag; that likely explains some of the long-context spike. We can share the test manifest.
- We did not change contract tiers; any sustained dedicated pool usage would be coming from our increased test traffic.

Attached a condensed usage export (acme_usage_breakdown.csv) and a pointer to our internal change log: reference id CHG-7739. Happy to join the Tuesday sync.

—Jordan
Jordan Pierce
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Cloud
(attachment: acme_usage_breakdown.csv)

On Mon, Sep 13, 2027 at 08:12 AM Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — attaching the draft monthly performance dashboard for Acme ...

I can owner the QBR readout bullet on "overall performance summary" and present the customer-facing slide. Proposed owners below (one-line remediation):
- Latency: tessa_morgan — run targeted model-variant tracing, add KV cache warmup for heavy long-context endpoints.
- Cost: vivek_kulkarni — validate dedicated-pool scaling config and propose a burst policy to limit long-run reserved consumption.
- Uptime: irene_choi — RCA for autoscaler flapping + a short change-control checklist for future kernel updates.
- Usage: laura_bennett — annotate dashboard with session-normalized metrics and call out synthetic test impact.

I flagged cost spikes in the dashboard comments (sheet tab: cost_notes). If the dedicated pool is the root cause, we should propose simple quota caps and a one-time credit request if Acme's test caused an operational overrun.

I'll slot the customer-facing deck and do a dry-run Wed 9/15 11:00 PT if that works for everyone.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, Jordan Pierce <jordan.pierce@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance dashboard handoff + QBR checklist and owner assignments

Thanks — quick status from infra: 
- Early look at autoscaler logs shows repeated scale-down/scale-up cycles during the rolling kernel update window on 9/10. Root cause - a health-probe timeout exacerbated by a temporary network hiccup. Fix: increase probe timeout and gate kernel restarts behind a node drain window. I can roll a config change as a canary to one pool tomorrow.
- Cost: preliminary breakdown shows 18% of the month-over-month cost delta is due to long-context requests (token volume), ~14% appears attributable to a misconfigured reserved burst policy in region-us-west. I'll have a detailed delta by EOD tomorrow and a recommended burst cap.

If Acme's soak tests are responsible for the rest of the spike, we should coordinate a quota cap for tests next billing cycle. Jordan — can you confirm expected peak qps for your test?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

On Mon, Sep 13, 2027 at 11:45 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — quick status from infra: ...

RCA draft for the two short incidents (to include in the QBR appendix):
- Incident 2027-09-04 (5m): external network jitter during a cross-region sync; autoscaler retries caused momentary 502s. Mitigation: improve probe thresholds for transient network errors.
- Incident 2027-09-10 (12m): rolling kernel update combined with immediate node restart; health-probe timeout surfaced due to transient IO latency. Mitigation: add node-drain window and gate kernel restarts with graceful drain.

Checklist for QBR slide (short bullets):
- Owners confirmed: latency (Tessa), cost (Vivek), uptime (Irene), usage (Laura).
- Action items with dates: Vivek -> burst-cap proposal (09/14 EOD), Tessa -> trace artifacts (09/14 noon), Irene -> final RCA (09/14 10:00), Laura -> deck dry-run (09/15 11:00).
- Customer ask: Jordan to confirm soak-test peak QPS and whether any synthetic runs are scheduled before the QBR.

I can take the 14:00 PT sync and run the short 30-min alignment.

Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Director, Reliability
